newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Sept 17.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Sept 17.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Tuesday morning.
** Light volumes seen as Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) remains closed for second straight day on local religious festival. The National Stock Exchange (NSE) is open for trade.
** Indian stock markets expected to slide this week on fears of economic slowdown and sluggish growth in corporate earnings, brokers and analysts say

Last week, Bombay's benchmark 30-share index slumped 160.70 points or 4.8 percent to 3347.37 after the government failed to deliver anticipated tax reliefs, including a waiver of a minimum corporate tax proposed in the government's July budget

** Indian Oil Corp (IOC) plans to make a 10 billion rupee quasi-equity offer during the current financial year. The issue will be a mix of non-convertible debentures and warrants. IOC plans to utilise the issue proceeds to part finance its on-going and future projects, the Business Standard newspaper reports
** The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) arrests former communications minister Sukh Ram on his arrival from London, the Times of India newspaper reports

Earlier, Sukh Ram claimed that about 40 million rupees, recovered by the CBI during raids on his residences in India, belonged to the Congress party. He said the money was part of funds raised by the party for electioneering. The party denied the accusation

** Government relaxes investment norms for private provident, superannuation and gratuity funds. The statutory deployment in the Special Deposit Scheme has been brought down from 30 percent to 20 percent, the Financial Express reports
** The 50-stocks National Stock Exchange (NSE) index .NSEI fell 19 points to close at 962 on Monday as punters and foreign funds offloaded select stocks
** Last Friday, the 30-share BSE index .BSESN closed 44.17 points or 1.3 percent lower at 3347.37
** The 100-share National index .NATEX fell 14.45 points or 0.95 percent to 1512.42 on Friday
** Belgian bank Banque Bruxelles Lambert said on Monday it struck a strategic cooperation accord with India's leading private bank Vysya Bank under which BBL will take a five percent stake in Vysya

The deal, which still has to be vetted by Reserve Bank of India, would also give BBL a seat on the board of directors. BBL said the deal would allow it to improve its service to clients dealing with India
